title: Vector Join
motivation: Vector joins — finding all query-data vector pairs within a distance threshold — are fundamental to vector and vector-relational databases powering multimodal retrieval and semantic analytics, yet state-of-the-art methods suffer from redundant index traversals and excessive distance computations.
goal: A unified framework for fast approximate vector joins: soft work sharing that reuses traversal results across queries, a merged index over query and data vectors, and an adaptive hybrid search strategy robust to out-of-distribution queries (arXiv:2603.16360).

title: Semantic Operators
motivation: Semantic operators (filter, join, group-by over unstructured data using LLMs) are powerful but expensive; existing engines optimize logical plans poorly and burn LLM calls where cheaper proxies would do.
goal: SAGE: a self-optimizing engine for semantic operators — analyze bottlenecks of SOTA engines, then replace expensive LLM calls with cheaper proxies such as vector embeddings and clustering, with accuracy guarantees.

title: NL2SQL
motivation: Natural-language interfaces to databases still fail on complex, real-world queries; the interesting failures lie beyond what a single LLM call can fix.
goal: An umbrella project combining LLM agents, DB execution feedback, RAG/TAG, approximate query processing, and finetuning — identify where SOTA baselines break, then attack those bottlenecks with the right combination of techniques.

title: AI-Driven Research Systems
motivation: AI agents can now write and revise code against execution feedback — can they act as autonomic researchers for database internals, and what infrastructure do they need to do so reliably?
goal: A testbed where AI agents generate physical query plans (implementing and connecting physical operators), run them, and self-revise from execution results and correctness tests — analyzing the gap against plans from existing database systems and distilling lessons into new optimizers.

title: Declarative & Adaptive Query Processing
motivation: Decades of query processing techniques (1981-today) remain fragmented; no single system adapts its execution to each query instance to approach the performance an oracle would achieve.
goal: Instance-optimal (cloud) DB through adaptive execution: measure the gap between a baseline and a virtual instance-optimal method, close it with recent and novel adaptive techniques, unified in a declarative framework.

title: Learned & Adaptive Cloud Indexing
motivation: Cloud databases face shifting workloads and data placement costs where static indexes are either wasteful or missing exactly when needed.
goal: Instance-optimality in the cloud via learned, adaptive indexing — build indexes incrementally and adaptively as queries arrive, approaching the performance of an ideal index chosen in hindsight.

title: Learned Query Optimization
motivation: LLMs and learned models promise better query optimization (including cardinality estimation), but current approaches need heavy training and offer little robustness.
goal: Benchmark LLM-based query optimization, then develop better methods using multi-path reasoning and self-reflection — minimizing training overhead, reliance on external models, and optimization latency.

title: LLM Inference Engines
motivation: LLM inference and serving engines (vLLM and friends) differ widely in mechanisms and performance, and no unified model explains their behavior across hardware and objectives.
goal: A unified performance model of LLM inference engines: measure and break down throughput/latency across hardware settings, model multiple engines in one framework, and identify bottlenecks and preconditions to harness future hardware.
